variants.title: Superconducting Tc by four-probe: a niobium film
variants.sample: Niobium film on sapphire, Tc near 9.2 K (SIMULATED)
variants.method: four-probe R against T, zero field and 0.2 T
variants.unknown: Tc, transition width, residual resistance ratio
variants.note: A clean elemental film: a sharp transition (width under 0.1 K) and a field of 0.2 T already lowers Tc by about 2 K, because Bc2 of niobium is only about 0.4 T. Tc of bulk niobium 9.25 K (Kittel); the film's Bc2, width and resistances are illustrative.

source.title: C. Kittel, Introduction to Solid State Physics, Table 10.1: Nb Tc = 9.25 K

variants.title: Superconducting Tc by four-probe: a lead wire
variants.sample: Lead wire, a type-I superconductor, Tc 7.19 K (SIMULATED)
variants.method: four-probe R against T, zero field and 40 mT
variants.unknown: Tc, transition width, residual resistance ratio
variants.note: A type-I superconductor: its critical field is the thermodynamic Bc = 80.3 mT at 0 K, so 40 mT moves Tc to Tc0 sqrt(1/2). The very large residual resistance ratio shows a pure metal. Tc and Bc are Kittel's table values; the resistances are illustrative.

source.title: C. Kittel, Introduction to Solid State Physics, Table 10.1: Pb Tc = 7.19 K, Bc = 803 G
